workflowHypotheses.title: Microsoft controlled file intake and archive
workflowHypotheses.goal: Detect the current state of a selected changed file and copy it to an explicit target location, without treating change notifications as a lossless change log.

stages.description: Receive Graph root-item updated notification as wake-up hint; validate clientState.
Hydrate latest state from saved delta cursor, traverse pages and select only a current item that still exists and has a file facet.

Download the file bytes only after checking the current item; if its version changed after delta hydration, re-fetch/reconcile. Apply a transfer-size limit and never log or persist the short-lived preauthenticated URL.
Copy downloaded file bytes to an explicit target path using resumable upload; file approval is outside this connector hypothesis.

failureControls: Persist deltaLink; handle expired cursor with full resync.
Deduplicate repeated notifications and renew subscriptions before 42,300-minute expiry.
No file processing/egress until tenant, path and retention policy are explicitly selected.
Skip deleted entries and folders; enforce a bounded transfer size; never log or persist the preauthenticated download URL; re-fetch and reconcile if the source version changed before download.
assumptions: Proposed end-user demand is not verified.
OneDrive/Graph app registration and tenant consent are approved.

Send selected non-sensitive business summary to an explicitly chosen Slack channel.

failureControls: Return HTTP 200 only after durably queueing accepted event; deduplicate on stored delivery Idempotency-Key and test whether provider redelivery preserves the key.
Respect Moneybird 10-retry policy and Slack method throttles.
Never include full financial contact details without explicit need and approved data retention.
The paid-state predicate is an Elsa workflow guard after invoice hydration; an invoice event alone is not proof of payment. Test Moneybird event-to-current-state mapping before use.
assumptions: This is a hypothesis, not evidence of demand or pilot approval.
Moneybird administration owner authorizes scopes; Slack workspace approves minimal scopes.
No cross-tenant or workspace-to-administration data association is inferred.

workflowHypotheses.title: GitHub issue signal to Jira work item
workflowHypotheses.goal: Route a selected GitHub issue event to an explicit Jira project, preserve cross-system links and avoid duplicate issue creation.

stages.description: Receive and HMAC-verify GitHub issue event for a selected repository installation.
Hydrate/filter current issue state; exclude pull requests when the user asked for issue-only handling.
Search for existing linked Jira issue in authorized project.
Create/update selected Jira work item with explicit cross-link and approved fields.

failureControls: Deduplicate by delivery ID and external issue URL; provide periodic reconciliation because GitHub does not auto-redeliver failed deliveries.
Do not create on ambiguous project/field mapping; require user-selected project and mapping.
Honor Jira rate limits and workflow/project permission errors.
assumptions: Cross-vendor mapping and demand are unvalidated.
Existing Elsa.DevOps.GitHub source inventory does not establish operation/test readiness.
Jira 3LO app and webhook API support are approved.

workflowHypotheses.title: Google Drive change to controlled Sheets audit row
workflowHypotheses.goal: Record selected Drive file metadata after change into a user-selected Sheet without broad mailbox/file access.

stages.description: Receive file notification and reconcile using Drive changes cursor.
Resolve current file metadata only for user-selected/shared-with-app files.
Append minimal file ID/name/change timestamp to a selected spreadsheet.

failureControls: Use drive.file and selected-resource consent where possible.
Drive notifications carry no resource details; cursor backfill handles missed notifications.

Use an application-owned durable work ledger keyed by file ID and observed version; append has no provider idempotency guarantee, so reconcile after ambiguous responses and serialize competing writers.
assumptions: Drive push channels and per-file sharing setup are acceptable to users.
Row-level triggers are excluded; this is a file-change flow only.

workflowHypotheses.title: Support ticket context and human escalation
workflowHypotheses.goal: Find contextual CRM record for a support ticket and route a ticket escalation with an internal note after an explicit policy decision.

stages.description: Select tickets matching a supported query and explicit instance/user permissions.
Look up minimal CRM context using a documented contact search and consented CRM scope.
Add only a private internal note/assignment after human or workflow policy approval.
Notify a chosen internal escalation channel without copying sensitive ticket contents.

failureControls: Do not expose contact/ticket body across tenant boundaries or Slack destinations.
Require admin-configured webhook trigger and verify delivery; scope OAuth to tickets/contacts.
Pause on uncertain contact match; never automatically send public customer reply.
assumptions: Event wiring and Zendesk plan access remain unverified.
HubSpot OAuth scope/data-access mismatch needs a security decision.

workflowHypotheses.title: Calendar event to workflow deadline
workflowHypotheses.goal: Create a selected calendar event from an approved workflow deadline with scoped user authorization and duplicate protection.

stages.description: An Elsa start event receives the requested calendar, time window and approval context; this is internal workflow initiation, not a Google Calendar trigger.
Check selected calendar and window for an existing idempotency marker.
Create only when workflow data is complete and user-selected calendar is writable.

failureControls: A durable per-calendar work ledger and serialized retries are required; a pre-search is advisory and does not prevent races or a timeout after provider commit, so reconciliation/duplicate handling must be designed.
No attendee invitation or conferencing operation is included in the first candidate scope.
Handle calendar ACL errors and OAuth revocation visibly.
assumptions: This is a low-side-effect candidate example; no demand validated.
OAuth scope and verification outcome depend on public application state.

The candidate workflow crosses three distinct connection/event designs. A single public request created in 2024 and closed in 2025 for Slack approval workflows is a historical demand lead only; it does not establish a current sponsor or comparative demand.

rankedRecommendation.sensitivity: Demand evidence is sparse and not calibrated: one Slack approval-workflow request created in 2024 and closed in 2025 exists, but it is not a current sponsor or volume measure; numeric demand remains null for every provider. Under the charter weights, each deep-provider total is shown for hypothetical demand scores 0, 2.5, and 5; the demand component changes a total by at most 1.5 points. The resulting intervals overlap for every candidate, so there is no robust numeric winner. Cohort sequence is a conditional validation order based on program scope, documented operation completeness, shared primitive reuse, and relative effort—not an empirical popularity ranking. Recompute the score if comparable verified demand arrives.
rankedRecommendation.effortAssumptions: Illustrative focused engineer-day ranges for one maintained module with selected operations, integration tests, docs and packaging; assumes reusable OAuth/connection, signature verification, webhook durability, rate-limit and sandbox infrastructure exists. If those shared primitives are absent, add a separate platform estimate before commitment. Ranges exclude provider approval delays, legal/security reviews, cloud hosting projects, broad operation coverage, attachments and support rotations. Low confidence until an Elsa maintainer reviews.
maintainerDecisions: Which pilot cohort has an authorized user sponsor and concrete workflow evidence?
Who owns shared OAuth credentials/connections, tenant isolation, token revocation and secret recovery?
Which event/webhook/reconciliation primitives are common platform investments, and who operates renewals?
Which provider data classes, residency commitments and retention defaults are acceptable in Elsa Cloud?
Will publicly distributed applications obtain provider verification, marketplace approval and required security assessments?
How should existing Elsa.Slack and Elsa.DevOps.GitHub be brought onto a shared connection model without breaking current users?
exclusions: No comparative demand inference from third-party directory listings. The single historical Slack request is reported separately and not converted to a numeric score.
